results.question: Why do the shoes that go with Gladias's robe slow him down when he has to run?
results.answer_as_shown: The shoes paired with the Veridian Privacy Robe are built with high heels to match the robe’s height and with deliberately uneven soles that randomize the wearer’s gait; those design choices make quick, efficient movement difficult, so when Gladias has to sprint they impede his speed[c1-b86].

results.question: Once the kids go off to Vil and Daia, what is Seila planning to do with her time?
Which menu number does Gladias usually order from the Dzego food truck?
results.answer_as_shown: Gladias habitually orders the “number ten” from the Dzego food truck[c6-b2][c1-b105]

results.question: During the thermodynamics lesson, why did Zei keep his Arctic Emperor joke to himself?
results.answer_as_shown: Zei held back because the joke was already obvious to the class—explaining it would be “bad form,” since most students were already thinking of the Arctic Emperor and were sharing a brief, collective amusement. [c2-b93]

results.question: What did the instructor say was wrong with Zei's arm after the attack on the class?
How did Zei place in the Minpentai game he played the night before the bombing?
How did Mov manage to find Gladias when lots of people nearby were wearing identical robes?
results.answer_as_shown: Mov relied on a pre‑existing trust link that let his local AI share Gladias’s whereabouts. Because Gladias had added Mov to his trust list a year earlier and never removed him, the AI was authorized to turn on location sharing when they were supposed to meet, letting Mov pinpoint Gladias even among a crowd of identical robes[c3-b12][c3-b13].

results.question: What first got Gladias interested in working on Steering?
results.answer_as_shown: Gladias’s first spark came from the civics lessons he took as a child, where he learned how Veridian voting determined things like the public‑aesthetics tax that directly affected developers and land‑tax revenue [c1-b20]. That early exposure to how the system worked later led him to take a “warm‑up” aesthetics vote and then a more consequential vote as an Acolyte in the Order of Steering [c1-b38].

results.question: According to Mov, why does the tax system go to such lengths to keep Keepers anonymous?
results.answer_as_shown: Mov says the tax system is built with cryptographic networks, random selection, anonymous discussion and privacy robes specifically to shield Keepers’ identities. A recent breach—when a Keeper’s views were exposed and her husband lost his job—showed how vulnerable they are, so anonymity is needed to prevent personal retaliation and keep the decision‑making process safe from manipulation. [c3-b23]

results.question: What is the giant pyramid at the southern edge of Pafogai Du really, and what is it used for?
results.answer_as_shown: The “pyramid” that dominates the southern edge of Pafogai Du isn’t a newly built monument at all—it’s a natural mountain that has been reshaped and refurbished to look like a massive stone pyramid. Inside the “pyramid” are extensive caves that have been turned into living quarters and workspaces; a segment of the Dzego government occupies the complex, alongside many major businesses, making the site a high‑cost hub of administration and commerce[c4-b48][c4-b49].

results.question: Why does Zei say a shield that can never be destroyed can't exist?
results.answer_as_shown: Zei argues that because the fundamental laws are time‑reversible, any object that can be built can also be undone by running the creation process backward. Therefore something that truly cannot be destroyed would have no reversible creation path and thus could not exist in the first place; any “invincible” shield must hide a weakness that could be exploited by reversing its construction steps. [c4-b13]

results.question: What does Mu caution Zei about just before the quarter-finals?
Watching the quarter-final from far away, what does Fin think Zei wants almost as much as winning?
results.answer_as_shown: Fin believes that, besides winning, Zei is driven almost equally by the desire to hear Bai beg. [c4-b119]

results.answer_as_shown: The provided excerpts don’t include a moment where Bai apologizes after the game, nor a line showing Zei asking her for anything in response.

results.question: Why can't Dzego just build its own all-seeing camera network to counter the Arctic surveillance?
results.answer_as_shown: D Zego can’t simply flood the city with omniscient cameras because the Arctics already have agents planted inside every agency; any system that can see “too much” would instantly become a tool for those spies to turn against the public [c5-b77]. The only way to keep a camera network safe is to embed heavy cryptographic checks, hardware attestations and random‑inspection processes that limit what data is ever revealed [c5-b78]. Without those safeguards, an all‑seeing network would be vulnerable to the very surveillance it’s meant to counter.

results.question: How is the entrance fee worked out at the economics institute Zei and Bai visit in Freetown?
results.answer_as_shown: The institute lists a fee formula that depends on two variables: it rises with the square‑root of the amount of time you remain inside, and it falls as your academic‑or‑intellectual reputation score goes up [c5-b40]. That reputation score is hard to earn—earned through serious work rather than cheap “zero‑knowledge” collateral—so a higher score reduces the charge [c5-b41].

results.question: What kind of project does Seila suggest Gladias could take on if he becomes a Keeper?
results.answer_as_shown: Seila hints that, as a Keeper, Gladias could work on a project to redesign or tweak the rubrics so they better support Dzego’s interests. [c5-b113]

results.answer_as_shown: The text only tells us that the new rule for the city final gave both contestants and their AIs … [c7-b65]; it does not explain the priests’ purpose in allowing that visibility.

They only note that Nine stepped forward, looked at the device briefly, and that the group later examined and destroyed it — there’s no explicit comment from Nine about why he didn’t think it was meant to spy on the Keepers. Consequently, the text doesn’t provide an answer to that question.

results.question: Why does Dzego disguise its training of future defenders as a game instead of just recruiting soldiers openly?
Why did Gladias stop chasing perfect marks at school?
According to Eighteen, why does publishing military-relevant designs openly matter so much for Dzego?
results.answer_as_shown: Eighteen argues that open‑source military designs are a “lifeline” for Dzego because the Dzegojan lack the ability to create proprietary high‑end technology; they excel at taking and adapting open‑source plans. When the United Cities made their programming languages and formal‑verification tools openly available, Dzego could adopt those methods and dramatically improve their defenses against Arctic sabotage. [c10-b147]

results.question: What did Zei, Fin and Bai see on their way up the mountain to the city final?
What did Vil offer Lily as a reward for doing better in civics?
results.answer_as_shown: Vil promises Lily a trip to Northglade if she scores above seventy‑five on her next civics test[c8-b120].

results.question: After his attack fell apart, how did Zei manage to come back and win the city final?
results.answer_as_shown: After his aggressive wall‑building attack collapsed, Zei shifted to a defensive, information‑lean strategy. He let his ship’s walls crumble, then relied on a pre‑published “spaceship” that already encoded every possible glider attack and used only a few decisive bits at the end to deploy the exact move he needed, turning the limited‑bandwidth channel into a winning play. This defensive‑first, precision‑bit finish let him outlast his opponent and be declared the winner of the city final. [c14-b85][c14-b87][c15-b102][c15-b104]

results.question: What did the Freetown charging companies do to the carmaker that refused to chip in for defense?
results.answer_as_shown: The charging‑station makers banded together and threatened to block Mogna’s vehicles from using their network—effectively locking Mogna’s cars out of about ninety percent of Freetown’s charging stations unless the carmaker contributed to defense, which led to Mogna’s collapse. [c10-b24]

results.question: How can Den's hand device tell that a gadget answering it is really nearby and not relaying answers from somewhere else?
results.answer_as_shown: Den’s hand device runs an ultra‑fast challenge‑response protocol: it pings the target device millions of times and demands that the entire exchange finish within a tenth of a tick. That tiny deadline limits signal travel to roughly fifty light‑feet (about 13 m), so any reply that meets the timing must come from a gadget that is physically nearby rather than being relayed from elsewhere. [c9-b133]

results.question: How does the network Den showed Zei hide who sent a message?
results.answer_as_shown: Den explains that the mixnet wraps each message in three successive encryption layers. The first‑layer node strips only the outer layer, learns the address of a second‑layer node, and passes the still‑encrypted payload onward. The second node does the same for the middle layer, revealing the address of a third node. Only the third node removes the final layer, exposing the destination and the (still‑encrypted) payload. Because the three nodes are randomly chosen, an observer would need all three to collude to trace the sender, which makes the sender’s identity hidden. [c9-b115][c9-b116][c9-b117][c9-b118][c9-b119][c9-b120][c9-b121]

results.question: If payments in Veridia are private, how does the government make sure shops actually pay sales tax?
results.answer_as_shown: Veridian sales‑tax is built into the payment protocol itself: when a customer pays, the transaction automatically routes the tax portion to the government in real time, even though the details stay hidden by zero‑knowledge proofs. Compliance is then enforced not by audits of records but by random spot‑checks—inspectors who observe orders and verify that the tax‑paying transaction type was used at the point of sale[c6-b138].

results.question: Why does Gladias tell Delwart he doesn't expect the Arctics to escalate, when he isn't sure?
Why didn't teaming three bots up against Zei on the train help them much?
results.answer_as_shown: The bots fared poorly because the three‑on‑one format was outside anything they had ever been trained to handle. Their models had no data on cooperating against a single opponent, so they made elementary errors and even interfered with each other’s “negentropy,” essentially sabotaging one another rather than mounting an effective joint defense. [c12-b10]

results.question: Why does Den send Zei back to Pafogai Du after the invasion?
What interrupted the family dinner at the restaurant, and how did Seila react?
results.answer_as_shown: The dinner was cut short when Febric suddenly left the restaurant, running out to get to school after Gladias paid the bill [c6-b124][c6-b125][c6-b126]. The passages do not record any specific reaction from Seila to that interruption.

results.question: What advice did Zei pass along for the Arctic soldier smuggling messages?
How did Deluin beat Kau in the other semifinal?
results.answer_as_shown: Deluin won by playing a defensive, wall‑building strategy. He poured his resources into the rock formations at the north and northeast edges to erect strong walls, while also launching gliders that seeded “eternal glider factories” aimed southward. He never built mobile, symbol‑carrying ships, instead relied on his walls to reflect the gliders that Kau’s factories produced. Over thousands of turns Kau was forced to retreat behind the southern shrine and, as stray gliders and debris accumulated, his position collapsed, while Deluin’s fortified walls kept him safe and ultimately secured the victory[c14-b90][c14-b91][c14-b92][c14-b93][c14-b94].

results.question: What did Mov find out when he followed Delwart after the overheard meeting?
results.answer_as_shown: Mov learned that Delwart had gone to a follow‑up meeting with another Keeper. By positioning himself in the adjacent booth, Mov was able to pick up the conversation through the vibrations traveling through the wall[c13-b30][c13-b31].

results.question: How does the championship keep a player from finding out the day's rule change before their match?
results.answer_as_shown: The championship isolates the contestants and strips them of any means to look up the rule in advance. They sit in a “longhour” without internet, and are explicitly forbidden to bring hand devices or watches; only a robot will fetch them when the match is about to start, and the rule is only revealed then[c12-b133][c12-b134].

results.question: How do the shrines work in the semifinal version of Minpentai?
results.answer_as_shown: In the semifinal (hex‑grid) match, the shrines can be converted into “eternal glider factories.” If a glider reaches the space just beyond a shrine after exactly two intervention turns, it triggers the shrine to launch a continuous glider stream that bounces back and forth; each collision breaks off rock that sprays additional gliders northward, and the rock resets only after about a thousand turns [c14-b38]. Zei’s strategy therefore placed his ships so they could fire gliders into the shrines, turning the center‑south and center‑west shrine pairs into permanent glider generators that fed his storm [c14-b53].

results.question: How do Keepers in a meeting keep each other from knowing who they are?
results.answer_as_shown: The system is built so that Keepers are anonymous to one another—identity information is deliberately hidden by the opaque design of the Veridian Steering and other bodies, which use random, secret committees and prevent participants from learning each other’s names or personal thoughts[c7-b130]. This intentional secrecy means they must keep their own thoughts concealed even from fellow Keepers[c7-b132].

results.question: Who is the woman who greets Zei at the train station in the capital?
results.answer_as_shown: The woman who greets Zei at the train station is the lead priest of Sadzu Du, an older woman about the same age as Mu, who introduces herself as Su, one of the nationals’ organizers[c12-b14][c12-b16].

results.question: How did Bai gather her information on the other championship players?
results.answer_as_shown: Bai’s insight comes from watching the opponents’ actual play. She observed that, across qualifying rounds, practice matches and the Gun‑vs‑Deluin game, the other contestants repeatedly rushed their moves—prioritising speed over strategy—because the scoring system rewards quick wins. From this pattern she concluded they’re “way too impatient” and advised Zei not to rush. [c14-b22][c14-b23]
